beats.text: If my laptop breaks tomorrow, can someone else run this project, and get exactly the same result? In ML, this idea has a name. Reproducibility. And today's ticket is all about it.

beats.text: See, why does it matter so much in ML? Let's say our model says, tomorrow will be Poor, keep the children inside. And someone asks, how did you get this answer? beats.text: As Java developers, we already know this very well. Nobody writes a controller before the project has its structure and its pom.xml. beats.text: So reproducibility stands on four simple ideas. Let's take them one by one.

v3.text: So reproducibility stands on four simple ideas. Let's take them one by one.

beats.text: Idea one. Every project lives in its own room. Just think once. On one laptop, I have many Python projects. One needs a new version of a library, another one needs an old version. If they all share one Python, upgrading for one project silently breaks the other. So each project gets its own isolated environment. In Python, we call it a virtual environment.

beats.text: Because in Java, Maven already does it for you. It keeps every library version separately, and each project picks exactly what it needs. Python, by default, has one shared shelf for everyone. The virtual environment gives every project its own shelf. Same idea, different tool.
